options: Blowing dust out of the system unit
Updating the antivirus and operating system

options: Even lighting without glare on the screens
A bright light shining directly onto the screens

options: Fitting air conditioning, keeping windows closed and covering equipment when not in use
Sweeping the floor with a dry broom while the computers are running
Leaving the windows open for fresh air

questions.explanation: Programmers write, test and maintain programs.

questions.explanation: Data processing staff must keep personal information confidential.

options: a disease that affects computer users
a program that can damage data and spread to other computers

options: Infected flash drives and e-mail attachments

The computer becomes unusually slow and files disappear

questions.stem: The way records are arranged on a storage medium is called

questions.explanation: Tape can only be read in order, so it suits serial and sequential files.

options: both in sequence and directly by using an index
only one after the other from the beginning
questions.explanation: The index allows direct access while the records remain in key order for sequential processing.

questions.stem: Converting data into a coded form to prevent unauthorised people from reading it is
questions.explanation: Encryption protects data by making it unreadable without the key.

questions.stem: The person responsible for managing a database, its security and user access rights is the
questions.explanation: The DBA controls the database, access permissions, backups and performance.

questions.stem: Giving some users permission only to read records while others can edit them is an example of
questions.explanation: Access control limits what each user can do with the data.

questions.stem: A database whose data is stored at several sites connected by a network but appears as one database to users is a
questions.explanation: Distributed databases spread data across sites while users see one system.

options: each branch can keep its local data close by, and the system can continue if one site fails
all data must be kept on one computer only
it removes the need for a network
it cannot be accessed by branch staff

using several processors and disks to work on queries at the same time
allowing only one user at a time

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the main features of the first and third generations of computers under the headings: (i) basic component; (ii) size; (iii) speed. [6 marks]
(b) Convert the decimal number 45 to binary. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) first generation: vacuum tubes; very large (room-sized); slow (milliseconds)
3 marks: (a) third generation: integrated circuits; smaller (minicomputers); faster (nanoseconds)
2 marks: (b) correct working by repeated division by 2 (remainders 1,0,1,1,0,1)
2 marks: (b) 45 = 101101 in binary
questions.explanation: First generation computers used vacuum tubes, were huge and slow. Third generation used integrated circuits, were smaller and much faster. 45 / 2 gives remainders 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1 read upwards: 101101.

questions.stem:
(a) Define information processing. [2 marks]
(b) Describe four steps involved in information processing. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the conversion of data into meaningful information through operations such as collection, sorting, calculating and output
8 marks: (b) any four, 2 marks each: data collection; data preparation/validation; input; processing (sorting, calculating, merging); storage; output/dissemination
questions.explanation: Information processing turns raw data into useful information. Steps: collect data, prepare and validate it, input it, process it (sort, calculate), store it, and output or distribute the results.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of networking. [2 marks]
(b) Distinguish between LAN and WAN. [4 marks]
(c) Distinguish between the Internet and an intranet. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) linking two or more computers so that they can share data and resources
2 marks: (b) LAN covers a small area such as a building, is privately owned and fast
2 marks: (b) WAN covers a large area such as a country or continent, often uses public telecommunication links
2 marks: (c) Internet is a public worldwide network open to everyone
2 marks: (c) intranet is a private network of an organisation using Internet technology, open only to authorised users
questions.explanation: Networking is linking computers to share resources. A LAN covers a building; a WAN covers countries. The Internet is public and global; an intranet is private to one organisation.

questions.stem:
The principal of a school in Owerri wants to keep student records in MS Access.
(a) Define a database management system and give two examples. [4 marks]
(b) Describe the steps involved in creating a table called STUDENTS with the fields AdmNo, Surname, Class and DateOfBirth. [8 marks]
(c) Suggest, with reasons, the most suitable data type for each of the four fields. [4 marks]
(d) State which field should be the primary key and why. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) software used to create, store, retrieve, manage and control access to a database
2 marks: (a) any two: MS Access, Oracle, MySQL, dBase, SQL Server
2 marks: (b) start MS Access and create a new blank database, giving it a name
2 marks: (b) open the table in Design View
2 marks: (b) type the field names AdmNo, Surname, Class and DateOfBirth and choose a data type for each
2 marks: (b) set the primary key and save the table as STUDENTS
1 mark: (c) AdmNo: short text (or number) - an identification code
1 mark: (c) Surname: short text - letters
1 mark: (c) Class: short text - e.g. SS3A
1 mark: (c) DateOfBirth: date/time - allows date checks and sorting
2 marks: (d) AdmNo
2 marks: (d) it is unique for every student, so it identifies each record
questions.explanation: A DBMS (e.g. MS Access, Oracle) manages databases. Create a blank database, open a table in Design View, enter the field names and types, set AdmNo as primary key and save as STUDENTS. Types: AdmNo text/number, Surname text, Class text, DateOfBirth date/time. AdmNo is the key because it is unique.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between hardware maintenance and software maintenance, giving one example of each. [4 marks]
(b) State three precautions to take when charging or replacing the battery of a laptop or UPS. [3 marks]
(c) Explain what is meant by a computer crash and state two ways of recovering data after it. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) hardware maintenance: care of physical parts, e.g. cleaning the system unit, replacing a faulty part
2 marks: (a) software maintenance: keeping programs in good condition, e.g. updating antivirus, installing patches, removing unwanted programs
3 marks: (b) any three: use the correct charger; do not overcharge; replace with the correct battery type; switch off before replacing; keep away from heat; dispose of old batteries safely (1 mark each)
1 mark: (c) a crash is a sudden failure of a program, the operating system or the hard disk so that the computer stops working
2 marks: (c) any two: restore from backup; use data recovery software; use system restore; take the disk to a recovery specialist (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: Hardware maintenance looks after the physical parts (cleaning, replacing); software maintenance keeps programs updated. Use the right charger and battery type, avoid heat and switch off before replacing. A crash is a sudden failure; data can be recovered from backups or with recovery software.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the correct sitting arrangement for a computer user. [4 marks]
(b) State three reasons why liquids and food should be kept away from a computer room. [3 marks]
(c) State three ways of keeping a computer room free of dust. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) any four: sit upright with back supported; feet flat on the floor; eyes level with top of the monitor; arms at about 90 degrees with wrists straight; monitor about an arm's length away (1 mark each)
3 marks: (b) any three: spills can cause short circuits; may cause electric shock; crumbs damage keyboards; attract insects/rodents that damage cables (1 mark each)
3 marks: (c) any three: use air conditioning and keep windows closed; cover equipment when not in use; vacuum regularly; use doormats or remove shoes; avoid chalkboards (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: Sit upright with back supported, feet flat, eyes level with the top of the screen and wrists straight. Liquids and food cause short circuits, shocks and attract pests. Air-conditioning, dust covers and regular vacuuming keep dust out.

questions.stem:
(a) Define a computer virus. [2 marks]
(b) Give two examples of computer viruses or malware. [2 marks]
(c) State three ways a computer can become infected with a virus. [3 marks]
(d) State three ways of preventing virus infection. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) a malicious program that attaches itself to files, copies itself and can damage data or the system
2 marks: (b) any two: worm, Trojan horse, ransomware, boot sector virus, macro virus, spyware (1 mark each)
3 marks: (c) any three: infected flash drives; e-mail attachments; downloads from unsafe sites; pirated software; infected networks (1 mark each)
3 marks: (d) any three: install and update antivirus; scan removable media; avoid unknown attachments; use a firewall; avoid pirated software (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: A virus is a self-copying harmful program. Examples include worms, Trojans and ransomware. Infection comes from flash drives, attachments, unsafe downloads and pirated software; prevention includes updated antivirus, scanning, firewalls and caution with attachments.

questions.stem:
The tables below are part of a school database.
STUDENT (AdmNo, Surname, ClassCode)
CLASS (ClassCode, ClassName, FormTeacher)
(a) Explain the following terms with reference to the tables: (i) entity; (ii) attribute; (iii) primary key; (iv) foreign key. [8 marks]
(b) Identify the primary key of each table. [2 marks]
(c) State the type of relationship between CLASS and STUDENT and explain your answer. [4 marks]
(d) Write an SQL statement to list the surnames of all students whose ClassCode is 'S3A'. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) entity: a thing about which data is stored, e.g. STUDENT or CLASS
2 marks: (a)(ii) attribute: a property of an entity stored as a column, e.g. Surname
2 marks: (a)(iii) primary key: a field that uniquely identifies each record, e.g. AdmNo
2 marks: (a)(iv) foreign key: a field in one table that refers to the primary key of another, e.g. ClassCode in STUDENT
1 mark: (b) STUDENT: AdmNo
1 mark: (b) CLASS: ClassCode
2 marks: (c) one-to-many
2 marks: (c) one class has many students but each student belongs to only one class
2 marks: (d) SELECT Surname
2 marks: (d) FROM STUDENT
2 marks: (d) WHERE ClassCode = 'S3A';
questions.explanation: Entities are STUDENT and CLASS; attributes are their columns. AdmNo and ClassCode are primary keys; ClassCode in STUDENT is a foreign key. CLASS to STUDENT is one-to-many. SQL: SELECT Surname FROM STUDENT WHERE ClassCode = 'S3A';

questions.stem:
(a) Define file organisation. [2 marks]
(b) Describe the following methods of file organisation: (i) serial; (ii) sequential; (iii) indexed sequential; (iv) random. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the way records are arranged and stored in a file on a storage medium
2 marks: (b)(i) serial: records stored one after another in the order they arrive, with no key order
2 marks: (b)(ii) sequential: records stored in order of a key field and accessed one after another
2 marks: (b)(iii) indexed sequential: records in key order with an index that allows direct access as well as sequential access
2 marks: (b)(iv) random: records stored at addresses calculated from the key and accessed directly
questions.explanation: File organisation is how records are arranged on a medium. Serial: in arrival order. Sequential: in key order. Indexed sequential: key order plus an index for direct access. Random: stored at calculated addresses for direct access.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the concept of data security. [4 marks]
(b) Describe three methods of protecting data in a database. [9 marks]
(c) State seven duties of a database administrator. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) protecting data from unauthorised access, corruption, theft or loss so that it remains confidential, accurate and available
3 marks: (b) access control: user names, passwords and permissions limit what each user can see or change
3 marks: (b) encryption: data are coded so that they cannot be read without the key
3 marks: (b) backup and recovery: regular copies kept elsewhere so data can be restored (or audit trails, firewalls)
7 marks: (c) any seven: design the database; grant and revoke user access; ensure security; make backups and recover data; monitor performance; maintain data integrity; install upgrades; train users (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: Data security means keeping data confidential, accurate and available. Methods: access control with passwords and permissions, encryption, and backups. The DBA designs the database, manages users and access, ensures security, backs up and restores data, maintains integrity and tunes performance.
